subject: Data locality decision & next steps — pilot scope and backup strategy
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@medicore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Data locality decision & next steps — pilot scope and backup strategy

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can lock the pilot scope: 

- High-level asks we heard: EU resident patient data must remain in EU for EU users; US patient traffic should stay within US regions. Medicore also needs a documented failover path for cross-region events and an RPO/RTO target for backups.
- Specifics requested from Redwood: support for region pinning per tenant, cross-region warm-standby failover, encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and retention/deletion controls for PII on request.

Attachments: I attached the Medicore data requirements you sent and a draft pilot scope (redwood-pilot-scope-v1.xlsx). Please review the quick items below and confirm so we can get the SOW and pilot schedule out: 

1) Residency confirmation: will Medicore require hard-region lock (no cross-border replication) for EU tenants, or is asynchronous geo-replication with encryption acceptable as long as data is logically pinned?
2) RPO/RTO targets: what are your target windows for production failover vs. backups (e.g., RPO 1h / RTO 4h)?
3) Snapshots & backups: do you require immutable snapshots for a retention window, or lifecycle-delete is acceptable?
4) Compliance docs: can you share the contact for procurement/legal to run a BAA and SOC2 evidence exchange?

Next steps I propose: we turn up the pilot in a single EU region (we recommend eu-central) with a warm standby in US-west for controlled failover testing. If that sounds right, we’ll schedule a tech-run with Vivek and provide a short runbook and sample configuration.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your replies and will follow up with a proposed timeline once we have the RPO/RTO constraints.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@medicore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Gomez <lucia@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 15:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data locality decision & next steps — pilot scope and backup strategy

Kimberly — really helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with ops/legal: 

- Residency: For EU patients we need region-locked storage (data must not be replicated outside EU for primary records). We can accept asynchronous replication for metadata/aux if encrypted and access-controlled, but primary PII must remain in-scope EU.
- Failover: We want a cross-region warm standby that can be promoted for up to 72 hours on DR events. The warm standby can be in another region (US-west) but must not contain unencrypted PII at rest unless under our KMS keys.
- RPO/RTO: Target RPO 1 hour, RTO 2-4 hours for the pilot scope (production SLAs can be tightened after).
- Snapshots: Immutable snapshots for 30 days are preferred for audit — we need tamper-evidence for those snapshots.
- Legal/procurement: Please loop in Redwood legal for a BAA and share a SOC2 report; procurement contact is Lucia Gomez (cc'd).

I attached an internal note with our retention policy excerpt. Also, rough budget question: can you give a ballpark monthly cost delta for EU-locked deployment + warm standby for a 3-node pilot? That will help us prep the purchase request.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director of IT Operations | Medicore Health
sanjay@medicore.com

Attachments: medicore-retention-excerpt.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@medicore.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data locality decision & next steps — pilot scope and backup strategy

Hi Sanjay — digging into the technical bits you asked about: 

- Region-locking: Redwood supports tenant-level region pinning. When you request EU region-locked storage we set the serving and persistent storage to eu-central (or chosen EU region) and block automatic replication of primary shards outside that region. Secondary metadata replication can be configured with fully encrypted transport.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and external HSM integrations for on-prem/private deployments. Keys can be enforced such that any replicated copy in a warm-standby is encrypted with your key; without key rotation the standby cannot decrypt.
- Warm standby & promotion: our warm standby model keeps KV cache primed and persistent state replicated asynchronously. Promotion time for a controlled failover (pre-validated) is typically 10–30 minutes for config + routing changes; full health checks and ingestion ramp to reach steady-state can be 1–3 hours depending on indexing and backlog. This aligns with your RTO target.
- Snapshots: We can produce immutable snapshots (Write Once storage) retained for the requested 30 days and provide verifiable hash-chaining for tamper evidence.
- Deletion/retention: We support tenant-scoped retention policies and on-demand data deletion APIs. For regulatory deletion (e.g., GDPR right to erasure) we recommend a documented workflow that includes last-snapshot retention for forensic needs, if required.

Open items for you: 
1) Confirm whether EU primary data must be physically unable to leave EU (hard legal restriction) vs. policy-level mitigation (we can log and block replication but the platform operator still controls physical movement in extraordinary cases).
2) Confirm the desired SLA for the pilot (we can offer a 99.9% uptime objective for pilot infra).

If you want, I can produce a one-page tech-run summary showing the pinning configuration and promotion steps.

—Vivek
Director, Product Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data locality decision & next steps — pilot scope and backup strategy

Thanks Vivek — and thanks Sanjay for the quick answers. Short bullet plan and next steps so nothing slips: 

- Pilot scope agreed: EU primary region-lock (eu-central) with warm-standby in us-west; RPO 1h, RTO target 2–4h, immutable snapshots 30 days.
- Security/compliance: Redwood to share SOC2 summary and KMS integration docs; Medicore to share signed BAA (we will route Redwood legal to execute).
- Deliverables before pilot start: tech-run doc (Vivek), runbook for promotion tests, cost estimate for 3-node pilot.
- Timeline: propose pilot kickoff week of Aug 7 — technical run Aug 8, configuration validation Aug 9–10, smoke failover test Aug 11. Please confirm if dates work for your ops team.

Action items for Medicore (quick): confirm the procurement contact for DocuSign (Lucia?), and confirm whether immutable snapshots must be stored in EU only or can be archived in US under encryption.

If we get confirmations today, I’ll send the statement-of-work draft and an initial cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly
